summary: The smart #5 is the brand's first mid-size SUV, a 4.7m, five-seat Geely SEA-platform sibling of the Zeekr 7X with a 94kWh usable battery, 800V charging and a 630-litre boot on every grade. CarExpert's overseas drive of the BRABUS called it a competent, likeable and comfortable electric SUV with a staggeringly roomy cabin, but found the flagship leans in corners and was thirsty at 24.0kWh/100km. No Australian outlet had driven it locally at launch, it is not yet ANCAP-rated, and LSH Auto sells it through only three east-coast showrooms.
pros: Pro+ costs $58,900, the same as the Tesla Model Y Premium RWD, but offers 590km WLTP range from a 94kWh usable battery against the Tesla's 466km
400kW DC charging on an 800V architecture is claimed to take 10-80 per cent in about 18 minutes, and every grade gets 22kW AC
Boot of 630 litres seats up and 1,530 litres folded, plus a front boot (72L on rear-drive grades per Chasing Cars), with rear seats that fold flat into a bed and 230V vehicle-to-load
1,600kg braked towing on all three grades, matching the smaller smart #1 and #3
Unconditional 5-year/150,000km vehicle warranty plus a separate 8-year/150,000km battery warranty with a 70 per cent state-of-health threshold
cons: LSH Auto Australia sells and services smart through just three showrooms (Melbourne, Sydney, Brisbane), with nothing in WA, SA, Tasmania, the ACT or the NT
Not yet rated by ANCAP; the five-star result is Euro NCAP's from 2025
BRABUS at $73,900 gives up 50km of WLTP range (540km) for 475kW that CarExpert called unnecessary, and leaned noticeably in corners on test
The heavy 100kWh pack costs efficiency: claimed 18.4kWh/100km on rear-drive grades and 19.9 on the BRABUS, which CarExpert saw rise to 24.0 on test
Smart cut #1 and #3 list prices by up to $5,000 within two years of launch, so early resale values on the #5 are a risk
